# Gene Tournament — Final Report (Sprint 3)

*Generated by `pipelines/gene_tournament/write_final_report.py` from the Sprint-3 artefacts in `reports/gene_tournament/`. Every table and number is read from a file; the prose is judgement. All work is computational. The chemistry gate is closed: nothing here is a target nomination, a direction of benefit, or a reason to intervene.*

> **CORRECTED 2026-09-23 (Sprint 3.1).** A correction pass audited this report's strongest claims; the original text below
> is kept unchanged and each affected paragraph carries its own dated block. Summary (full evidence in [`reports/sprint3_1/SYNAPTIC_RECON_REPORT.md`](sprint3_1/SYNAPTIC_RECON_REPORT.md)):
> (C1) no presynaptic skew — postsynapse is not weaker; the surviving core is synaptic-membrane /
> trans-synaptic adhesion. (C2) with propagated GO, neurodevelopmental sets also survive, so synaptic biology
> is not the *only* pathway signal. (C3, C4) conditioned runs had used a 17,069-gene universe and
> unpropagated GO. (C5, C6) "1.13x" is not identifiable and "121/159 same sign" was unsigned; a genuine
> allele-direction test gives 112/136 concordant. (C7, C8) NEGR1's 4 colocs are 1 independent unit;
> transcript-level eQTLs had been counted as gene-level (SYT1 0 qualifying); RPS26 meets the unchanged
> threshold on independent adult cohorts. (C9) "adult-modifiable" → ADULT-EXPRESSION-COMPATIBLE.
> (C10, C11) Top-50 ranks count one UK-Biobank lineage several times; a trailing-space bug counted a UKB
> study as UKB-free. (C12) DCC expression timing ≠ functional timing. (C13) the presynaptic voltage-gated
> channel set is driven by KCNJ3 (GIRK1).

## Headline

1. **The universe can be ranked, but only coarsely.** 375 of 18,418 genes pass Bonferroni in a verified gene-level analysis of general cognition (N=282,014); they are **159 independent loci**, not 375 findings. Beyond the first ~20 genes the consensus ranking is unstable: 39 of the top 50 have rank intervals reaching past 200, and ranks 51+ are ties.
2. **Extreme cognition is continuous with ordinary cognition at gene level.** The extreme-IQ sample (IQ~170) shows 1.13x the shift pure continuity predicts, 121/159 independent loci point the same way, and no gene is genome-wide significant in the tail. There is no genius gene set.

> **CORRECTED 2026-09-23 (Sprint 3.1).** (C5, C6) The 1.13x ratio spans 0.61–1.25 under plausible ascertainment/winner's-curse assumptions and cannot prove continuity; "121/159 point the same way" was an unsigned gene-level statistic. The defensible statement: no strong evidence for a distinct common-variant architecture — 112/136 testable lead SNPs have concordant allele direction in the extreme sample (P=4e-15), within the range continuity predicts.
3. **Synaptic biology is the only pathway signal that survives an unbiased, fully conditioned test** (6 of 6,200 sets at global FDR, all synaptic, presynaptic rather than postsynaptic). It reproduces in an overlapping meta-analysis and is untested — not refuted — in the only UKB-free sample. Myelin, energy metabolism, astrocytes, ion channels, GPCRs, neuromodulators, translation and chromatin do not survive.

> **CORRECTED 2026-09-23 (Sprint 3.1).** (C1, C2) Direct joint/contrast tests show no presynaptic skew (postsynapse ≥ presynapse; contrasts null); the robust core is synaptic-membrane / trans-synaptic adhesion. With GO propagated on the ontology, CNS neuron differentiation and neuron migration also survive global FDR in every covariate specification, so "the only pathway signal" is withdrawn.
4. **The gene-to-direction bridge does not exist yet.** 1,725 of 1,890 top locus-to-gene calls (91%) are driven by distance or gene density; only 34 genes have biology-driven fine-mapping support; and **zero** genes have a directionally consistent adult-brain expression effect at the pre-set threshold.
5. **The hand-picked seed list does not survive contact with the genome.** 1 of 25 testable seeds passes Bonferroni (CKB, rank 365). The strongest human loci — DCC, NEGR1, EXOC4, NT5DC2, BSN, MEF2C — were never on it.
6. **Three corrections to earlier sprints**: the Codex/Astra branch exists (Sprint 2 said it did not); the 2q12.3 duplication's gene list was wrong (wrong genome build); ADGRB1's Sprint-2 downgrade is reversed. Details in §H and the red-team section.

## A. Top 50 human cognition genes

Natural-intelligence ranking: **Robust Rank Aggregation** over the dimensions that have at least one gene passing their own multiple-testing threshold — direct cognition (MAGMA), independent replication, fine-mapping, brain colocalisation, positive human perturbation, module convergence. Eligibility: MAGMA gene FDR<0.05 (2,423 genes). One gene per LD block. Extreme-tail and arithmetic ranks are reported per gene but enter only the all-dimensions sensitivity run (see §Rank robustness for why, and when that rule was adopted).

*Rank gaps* occur where an LD block-mate outranks a gene (one gene per block is shown). *Fine-mapping*: the top L2G score and its dominant driver where a supported locus exists; "positional only" where every top call is driven by distance or gene density. *Ties*: several genes share rank 51 — synaptic-module members that the dimensions cannot separate. That is the resolution limit of the evidence. ## B. Top 50 adult-modifiable candidates

> **CORRECTED 2026-09-23 (Sprint 3.1).** (C9) "Adult-modifiable" is relabelled **ADULT-EXPRESSION-COMPATIBLE**: the gate is adult expression, which is not modifiability. See `reports/sprint3_1/adult_evidence_hierarchy.csv` (five tiers; no gene has ADULT_CAUSAL_EVIDENCE). (C11) All consensus ranks are triage: one UK-Biobank lineage feeds several dimensions (`reports/sprint3_1/rank_dependency_audit.csv`).

Same method, a different question. **Gate**: adult-expressed (GTEx v10, TPM≥1 in a brain tissue) and not prenatal-dominant or unknown in BrainSpan (1,593 eligible genes). Dimensions add adult-modifiability (developmental class + adult expression) and directionality. **Safety is a flag, never a promoting dimension.** "Adult-modifiable" here means *expressed and dynamic in the adult brain* — necessary for intervention, nowhere near sufficient. No row is a target.

The olfactory-receptor cluster (M10) is excluded as a gene-family artefact.

**Is any system consistently "more engaged" in high cognition?** Tested properly — module genes against *other cognition genes*, extreme-tail Z residualised on population Z — only the synaptic module is, nominally (P=0.012); it does not survive Bonferroni across 12 modules (P=0.144). A first version compared modules with the whole genome and credited every module with tail support; that was continuity inherited from gene selection and has been removed. "Enlarged" is not used: nothing here measures anatomy. Detail: [`module_report.md`](gene_tournament/module_report.md).

## D. Extreme-IQ commonality results

**MODE 2 — INDIVIDUAL-LEVEL COMMONALITY NOT COMPUTABLE WITH CURRENT ACCESS.** The only extreme-IQ case sample (Duke TIP, top ~0.03%, mean IQ ~170) has no public deposit (no dbGaP, no EGA); its controls are dbGaP-restricted (HRS, phs000428). Cohen's d, KS distance, AUC, odds ratios, EXTREME_COGNITION_COMMONALITY_50/90 and sibling-pair comparisons were **not computed, not approximated, not imputed**. [`extreme_tail_distribution_stats.csv`](gene_tournament/extreme_tail_distribution_stats.csv) records each quantity as not computable.

**MODE 1 — summary-statistic extreme rank (computed).** MAGMA on Zabaneh 2018 (GCST005626; 1,238 cases vs 8,172 controls, N_eff 4,300 — 65x less power than the population GWAS):

* Genome-wide significant genes in the extreme sample: **0**.
* Population-significant genes carry extreme-tail signal: mean Z 0.985 vs 0.333 (Mann-Whitney P=9.0e-26; gene-size-matched permutation P <0.0005 (0 of 2000 draws)).
* **Continuity test**: observed shift / shift predicted by pure power scaling = **1.13**. Locus-level sign test 121/159, P=9.2e-05.
* Rank correlation, one gene per LD block: rho=0.074 (P=1.3e-10) — weak, as 65x less power predicts.
* **Answer: continuous, not amplified.** Unresolved threat: HRS controls may overlap CHARGE cohorts in Davies 2018, which would bias toward this answer. Scope: common variants, European ancestry.

> **CORRECTED 2026-09-23 (Sprint 3.1).** (C5, C6) Replace with: no strong evidence for a distinct common-variant architecture in the extreme tail (signed locus-direction test 112/136, P=4e-15); magnitudes not identified; HRS overlap unresolved. See `reports/sprint3_1/extreme_tail_reassessment.md`.
* EXTREME_TAIL_AMPLIFICATION per gene is reported with its limitation: the top amplified genes (SLC25A1, COX18, ANKRD17 …) have population P>0.4 — with 18,000 genes and noise-dominated residuals, they are the expected extremes of a null. Hypotheses only. [`extreme_tail_rank.csv`](gene_tournament/extreme_tail_rank.csv)

## E. Math-specific results

* **math_specific: 0** · shared_g_math: 93 · general_only: 92 · unresolved: 18,156.
* **A (raw maths)**: the only open *objective* arithmetic phenotype is one timed UK Biobank item (FI4 positional arithmetic, N≈115k). **0 genome-wide significant genes**; correlation with general cognition rho=0.11. The Catalog's EFO "mathematical ability" is 0/12 on summary statistics and 99.8% of its associations come from one 23andMe paper of *self-report* and *course-taking*, reported separately and never pooled with the objective item.
* **B (maths with g)**: 93 genes are Bonferroni for g and nominally positive for arithmetic — shared_g_math — led by CEP57, FAM76B, MTMR2, GMPPB, RNF123, MGAT3, CAMKV, AMIGO3.
* **C (residual after g)**: the top residual genes are **keratins (KRT6B, KRT75, KRT6C)** — a chromosome-12 LD block, not maths biology. C never replaces A.
* **Answer**: math-specific genes are **not identifiable with open data**. The one g-orthogonal maths GWAS (2025, 53 SNPs) is built on restricted 23andMe data. [`math_gene_rank.csv`](gene_tournament/math_gene_rank.csv)

## F. Directionally resolved adult genes

Of 400 candidates queried in Open Targets (0 query errors): strong brain-QTL colocalisation with a **direct** cognition GWAS 20, moderate 71, weak 55, **EA-proxy-only 24**, none 0. Among brain colocalisations the fetcher labelled "cognition", EA traits outnumbered direct cognition ~2:1 and are excluded here.

**Direction resolved at the pre-set rule (≥3 strong gene-level brain eQTL/pQTL colocalisations, trait polarity applied, ≥80% sign agreement): 0 genes.** The first version read direction from each gene's single best colocalisation; for most genes that sign was contradicted by the gene's other brain colocalisations, so it was replaced. Near misses:

|---|---|---|---|
| NEGR1 | 4 | 75% |  |
| KANSL1 | 12 | 75% | 17q21.31 inversion haplotype: eQTLs of many genes share one signal; colocalisation is not gene-specific |
| CYP2D6 | 7 | 71% |  |
| RPS26 | 72 | 69% |  |
| SYT1 | 15 | 60% |  |
| ARL17B | 23 | 57% | 17q21.31 inversion haplotype: eQTLs of many genes share one signal; colocalisation is not gene-specific |
| IP6K2 | 3 | 0% |  |

NEGR1 (3 of 4, 75%) is the closest clean case; KANSL1 and ARL17B sit in the 17q21.31 inversion, where one haplotype drives many genes' eQTLs; RPS26 is a notoriously promiscuous eQTL. **The rule 'associated gene -> activate it' is not licensed for any gene in this tournament.** [`adult_brain_directionality.csv`](gene_tournament/adult_brain_directionality.csv)

> **CORRECTED 2026-09-23 (Sprint 3.1).** (C7, C8) NEGR1's four rows are ONE independent unit (one ROSMAP eQTL dataset × one multi-allelic indel lead, echoed by four overlapping UKB-containing GWAS): not near resolution. SYT1's 15 rows are all transcript-level (0 gene-level). Under strict gene-level eligibility counted on independent cohorts, RPS26 meets the unchanged threshold (4 adult cohorts, cognition-increasing allele → higher expression) — a ubiquitous ribosomal eQTL at a pleiotropic locus, tested in Sprint 4 Gate C, not a target. `reports/sprint3_1/negr1_qtl_independence_audit.csv`.

| Evidence | Class | Genes | Direction | Effect | Replication | Status |

| POSGEN:2q12.3_duplication | rare duplication (CNV) | EDAR|SH3RF3|SEPTIN10|SOWAHC | POSITIVE (higher cognition) | z=0.434 (~6.5 IQ points); p=7.58e-3; 36 carriers / 258,292 | none located | watchlist_unreplicated; nominal (not Bonferroni across 596 duplicated genes) |
| CODEX:RP02 | rare family variant | RIMS1 | reported enhanced verbal/executive performance in one kindred | single kindred | none; 2022 follow-up is Drosophila | hypothesis_only |
| CODEX:RP03 | common haplotype | KL | mixed | initial positive (n=718) vs large independent nulls (n=1,812; 320,861) | failed at scale | not_promoted |
| CODEX:RP04 | linkage + common SNP follow-up | unresolved (MOXD1 not promoted) | positive (exceptional memory families) | nominal SNP meta | nominal only | domain_lead_only |
| CODEX:RP05 | rare PTV burden | aggregate | NEGATIVE (loss of function lowers cognition/EA) | aggregate adverse burden | aggregate replicated | architecture evidence, NOT positive |

**The 2q12.3 duplication is the only positive-direction human perturbation in scope**, and its gene list is now correct: EDAR, SH3RF3, SEPTIN10, SOWAHC (hg19 chr2:109.51–110.38 Mb). Sprint 2 listed eight different genes from the hg38 cytoband. ClinGen has no dosage curation for any of the four — *unevaluated*, not benign. 41 Bonferroni cognition genes carry ClinGen dosage curation; **18 are haploinsufficient (score 3)**: ARID2, AUTS2, BCL11A, EXT1, FOXP1, GATAD2B, KANSL1, KMT2D, MEF2C, MYBPC3, QRICH1, RAD51C, RAI1, RPS26, SCN2A, SHANK3, SIX3, TCF20 — genes where losing one copy causes neurodevelopmental disorder. That is a safety signal, and it is never inverted into enhancement.

## H. Biggest surprises

1. **The Codex/Astra branch was real all along** — local, never pushed — and its X01 analysis was a genuine, well-documented MAGMA run whose gene-level layer this repository has now reproduced exactly. Sprint 2's "does not exist" was wrong because the search ran from a different clone.
2. **Continuity, quantitatively.** The extreme-IQ sample behaves almost exactly (1.13x) as the population polygenic score predicts. The tail is the same architecture turned up, not a different one.

> **CORRECTED 2026-09-23 (Sprint 3.1).** (C5) Withdrawn as a quantitative result; see the corrected headline 2.
3. **Presynaptic, not postsynaptic.** The surviving synaptic sets are presynaptic membrane, synaptic adhesion and presynaptic voltage-gated channels; the postsynaptic density — the home of the plasticity targets this project was seeded with — does not survive conditioning.

> **CORRECTED 2026-09-23 (Sprint 3.1).** (C1, C13) Withdrawn: postsynapse is not weaker in direct tests; the "presynaptic voltage-gated channel" set is driven by KCNJ3 (GIRK1, classically somatodendritic) and SCN2A.
4. **Locus-to-gene is mostly nearest-gene.** 91% of top L2G calls are driven by positional features.
5. **Constraint beats gene length.** Cognition signal concentrates in LoF-intolerant genes (partial rho=-0.108, P=2.3e-46, gene length removed) versus rho=0.058 for gene length itself.
6. **The 2q12.3 gene list was wrong** because a cytoband label was resolved on the wrong genome build.
7. **Cognition genes are neither developmental nor adult** as a class: prenatal/developmental OR 1.12 (P=0.190), adult-dynamic OR 1.25 (P=0.048).

Of the Codex nominations, **ADGRB1 passes** (P=1.6e-07, rank 238; Sprint-2 downgrade reversed), **GRM3 does not** (P=2.2e-05, rank 543), GABBR1 is null (rank 4,058). None of this is evidence against these genes as *drug targets* — gene-level association is silent on pharmacological modulation — but the seed list's claim to be grounded in human genetics does not hold.

## J. Highest-EV next analysis

**Test the six synaptic gene sets — and the continuity result — in a large cognition GWAS that excludes UK Biobank.** Every headline here rests on meta-analyses that share UKB, and the one UKB-free sample is 65x underpowered. A UKB-free replication would, in one computation, (a) convert the synaptic finding from reproducible to replicated or kill it, (b) test continuity without the HRS/CHARGE overlap threat, and (c) give every top gene its first independent gene-level test. Candidate inputs: CHARGE/COGENT components (application), or the within-sibship cognition GWAS (a free OpenGWAS registration — which also delivers Part F).

## Part S — the twenty questions

**1. Can the 4,459 cognition genes be meaningfully ranked?** Coarsely. 375 Bonferroni genes -> 159 independent loci; the top ~20 are stable-ish, the rest are not (rank intervals past 200 for most of the top 50; ties from rank 51). 40% of the swept 4,459 cannot be tested by the gene-based method at all (non-coding, non-autosomal).

**2. Which 50 genes are most consistently supported?** Table A. Led by DCC, NEGR1, EXOC4, NT5DC2, OGA, ERBB3, ATXN2L, CSE1L, LRRC37A, BSN — 0 pass the red team clean.

**3. Which genes are most shifted in extreme high-cognition individuals?** Individual-level: not computable. Summary-level: no gene is significant in the tail; the population-significant set as a whole is shifted (P=9e-26).

**4. Is extreme cognition continuous with population cognition at gene level?** Yes — 1.13x the power-scaling prediction; 121/159 loci same sign (P=9e-05). Caveats: sample overlap unresolved; common variants only.

> **CORRECTED 2026-09-23 (Sprint 3.1).** (C5, C6) Corrected answer: no strong evidence for a distinct common-variant architecture (signed test 112/136 concordant); the 1.13x ratio is not identifiable.

**5. Which genes are shared between g and mathematics?** 93 shared_g_math genes (objective arithmetic item nominal + g Bonferroni), led by CEP57, FAM76B, MTMR2, GMPPB, RNF123. Weak evidence: the maths side is one noisy item.

**6. Which genes appear math-specific?** None. The top residuals are keratins (an LD artefact).

**7. Which genes survive within-family evidence?** Not computable: within-sibship cognition data need an OpenGWAS registration and contribute 0 Catalog associations. Absence of measurement, not a verdict.

**8. Which genes have directionally resolved adult brain QTL support?** None at the pre-set rule. Closest: NEGR1 (3/4 concordant).

> **CORRECTED 2026-09-23 (Sprint 3.1).** (C7, C8) NEGR1 is 1 independent unit, not near resolution; RPS26 meets the unchanged rule under strict gene-level eligibility on independent cohorts (Sprint-4 Gate-C test case).

**9. Which are predominantly developmental?** Among the natural top 20: DCC, EXOC4, NT5DC2, CSE1L, SEMA3F, ALMS1, MEF2C, DBN1, TET2, NKAIN2. A developmental gene can explain natural variation and still be a poor adult lever.

**10. Which are genuinely adult-dynamic?** NEGR1, ERBB3, BSN, PDE1C, PEF1, SYT1, DDN, DHRS11, COL16A1, EEA1, KCNJ3, CDH9 — adult-dynamic in EXPRESSION, which is necessary for, not evidence of, modifiability.

**11. What top 10 biological modules emerge?** Table C: synaptic; transcription factors; RNA binding/splicing; chromatin; mitochondrial/translation; kinases; ubiquitin; transport; cell cycle; immune/MHC-adjacent.

**12. How much evidence do the top 5/10/20 modules capture?** 72% / 97% / 97% of FDR<0.01 gene-level evidence (NOT heritability) — the latter figures near-tautological because clustering assigns almost every gene.

**13. Is there a small plausible biological control set?** No. Only one module meets the evidence bar, so set cover returns one gene (NEGR1 adult-active; DCC any timing). Network hubs track annotation depth (rho=0.61). No directed causal graph exists, so controllability cannot be computed meaningfully.

**14. Which prior favourite genes disappear?** Table I: 24 of 25 seeds; PDE4B, GPR158, GABRA5, HCN1, GRM5, CRTC1, EIF2S1 notably.

**15. Which previously unknown genes rise to the top?** DCC, NEGR1, EXOC4, NT5DC2, OGA, ERBB3, ATXN2L, CSE1L, LRRC37A, BSN, PDE1C, PEF1, SEMA3F, SYT1, ALMS1, MEF2C, DBN1, TET2, NKAIN2, CTNNA2 — none was a seed.

**16. Does synaptic biology survive an unbiased test?** Yes — the only survivor (presynaptic/adhesion, not postsynaptic). Reproduced in an overlapping meta-analysis; not yet independently replicated.

> **CORRECTED 2026-09-23 (Sprint 3.1).** (C1, C2) Yes — as broad synaptic enrichment concentrated in membrane/adhesion genes, not presynaptic; and not the only survivor once GO is propagated.

**17. Does myelin survive?** No as a GO process (P=0.16). Oligodendrocyte-lineage expression is nominal in joint models across both atlases — unresolved.

**18. Does energy/metabolism survive?** No (OXPHOS P=0.37; 0/11 mitochondrial sets nominal).

**19. Does astrocyte biology survive?** No (GO sets null; cell-type result inconsistent across atlases and models).

**20. Which one analysis should be done next?** Section J: UKB-free replication of the synaptic sets and of continuity.

## Data access limitations

* No individual-level genotypes of any kind (Mode 2, rare variants, custom phenotypes).
* Within-sibship statistics behind OpenGWAS authentication; not registered for.
* EA and maths GWAS at full power require 23andMe agreements; public EA4 is 25% of the headline N.
* Davies 2018 general cognition is the open subset (5 cohorts removed); GTEx full nominal eQTLs are requester-pays; MetaBrain is form-gated.
* All gene-level statistics are European-ancestry; ancestry sensitivity is not computable.

## Restricted datasets that would materially improve the result

1. **Within-sibship cognition GWAS** (Howe 2022; free OpenGWAS registration) — Part F, and a partly UKB-independent test.
2. **CHARGE/COGENT cohort-level cognition statistics** (application) — UKB-free replication (§J).
3. **Duke TIP extreme-IQ genotypes + HRS controls** (collaboration + dbGaP) — Mode 2 and rare-variant burden.
4. **23andMe maths summary statistics** (qualified-researcher agreement) — the only powered maths phenotype.
5. **MetaBrain cis-eQTL** (form) — the largest brain eQTL resource, for direction.

## Numbers

* Genes evaluated: 9,221 Catalog gene strings (6,743 with direct-cognition evidence, 3,741 strict, 2,478 proxy-only); 18,418 genes in the gene-based test; 4,459 in the Sprint-2 sweep (2,668 testable by MAGMA).
* Studies: 419 classified — 120 direct-strict (≤49 independent cohort units), 176 clinical/ageing, 6 MTAG, 24 excluded as EA-derived or cross-trait, 93 proxy.
* Surviving each filter: FDR<0.05 2,435 → FDR<0.01 1,272 → Bonferroni 375 (159 loci) → Bonferroni in both Davies and Savage 264 (115 loci) → biology-driven fine-mapping 34 genes → strong direct-cognition brain coloc 20 → direction resolved 0 → red-team clean 0 (natural) / 1 (adult).
* Pathways: 12,400 set tests; global FDR<0.05: {'cond_annotation': 6, 'plain': 17}.
* Comparative (Part R, orthology availability only): 30 of 83 top genes queried successfully; the rest are NOT_QUERIED or failed (Ensembl REST errors) — never recorded as absent orthologues. Selection and convergence NOT computed (no species tree or trait covariates yet; corvids, parrots, orca and octopus absent from Compara).

## Rank robustness

* **Natural list**: RRA vs Borda top-50 overlap 21/50; primary vs all-dimensions 25/50; rank-interval upper bound >200 for 39/50; on the Pareto front 11/50; carried by: {'replication': 12, 'module': 12, 'direct': 11, 'finemap': 8, 'coloc': 7}.
* **Adult list**: RRA vs Borda top-50 overlap 26/50; primary vs all-dimensions 30/50; rank-interval upper bound >200 for 39/50; on the Pareto front 23/50; carried by: {'adult_modifiability': 14, 'module': 11, 'finemap': 10, 'direct': 6, 'replication': 5, 'coloc': 4}.
* **A design error, found and fixed, disclosed**: the first aggregation used all dimensions. Extreme-tail and arithmetic ranks — which have *zero* genes at their own significance threshold — carried 30 of the top 50, because RRA rewards a single extreme rank; and LoF tolerance (a safety property) promoted weakly associated genes into the adult list. The rule "a dimension enters the primary aggregation only if at least one gene passes its own multiple-testing threshold; safety is a flag" was **adopted after observing that run**. The all-dimensions ranks remain in every row for comparison.
* Monte Carlo: two runs of the same MAGMA analysis flip 4 genes across the Bonferroni line.
* Window: 91 of 375 Bonferroni genes change call at a 0 kb window.

## Blockers

* No UKB-free, adequately powered cognition GWAS in open access (blocks independent replication).
* Within-family data require a registration this project does not make on its own authority.
* No directed causal gene graph exists, so controllability analysis is not meaningful.
* Ensembl Compara REST is intermittently failing; Part R is partial.
